page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.2-32 is a memory-oriented virtual machine instance built on the Arm64 architecture. It is powered by an Ampere AmpereOne-M processor operating at a dedicated 3.6 GHz clock speed. The instance is configured with 4 physical cores mapping to 4 vCPUs via a single-thread-per-core layout, eliminating the resource competition typical of simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 32.0 GB, establishing a generous memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per physical core.

The hardware configuration does not bundle local disk storage, necessitating the use of remote network block volumes for boot disks and persistent data storage. Graphics accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs provisioned. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Architectural considerations require workloads to support 64-bit Arm execution, and I/O-heavy applications must factor in latency associated with network-attached block storage rather than direct-attached solid-state drives.

Resource allocation provides predictable single-threaded CPU execution coupled with high memory density. This design ensures consistent compute throughput and memory capacity without the overhead of unneeded GPU hardware. The instance functions effectively for in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, web serving frameworks, enterprise Java applications, and backend microservices compiled for Arm64 architectures.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.2-32 is an Arm64 compute instance designed for memory-intensive workloads requiring dedicated processor resources. Powered by an Ampere AmpereOne-M CPU clocked at 3.6 GHz, the configuration delivers 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs with one thread per core, avoiding multithreading contention. The instance is provisioned with 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per-core ratio that fits elevated memory requirements. No local storage or hardware GPUs are bundled with this shape, meaning persistence must be handled via attached remote block storage volumes. One complimentary public IPv4 address is provided for external network access. The instance offers predictable core execution and consistent memory capacity, making it technically suitable for in-memory databases, web serving tiers, containerized microservices, and general backend data processing tasks built for Arm64 architectures.
